name: Apache Maven
client: Maven 3 image / Temurin 27; compatibility Maven 3.9 image / Temurin 26 (exact bundled versions in CI logs)
auth: Use an access or reference token as the HTTP Basic password, with AW_USER equal to its subject. The subject needs read permission for installation and deploy permission for publication on the selected repository; token scopes cannot exceed that identity. The same clients also accept a user password when Basic password authentication is enabled. Use HTTPS.
fresh_home: Run in a new disposable pinned Maven container for every client session; also use distinct publisher-m2 and consumer-m2 under AW_WORK. This isolates Maven global settings, the Java user home, local artifacts and credentials.
prerequisites: Export AW_USER and AW_TOKEN; AW_USER must match the token subject.
A valid Maven project with group/artifact/version and configured build plugins.

configure.note: Maven interpolates the exported environment at invocation; settings.xml does not contain the token literal. Repository id aw must match the deployment or resolution repository id.

publish.note: Publish to a local or one-node federated repository. Remote repositories are read-through caches; select the local deployment member when reading through a virtual.

steps.note: Run in a valid Maven project with a pinned deploy plugin. package then deploy:deploy avoids installing the artifact into the consumer local cache.

install.note: Select a local, remote, virtual or one-node federated repository with read permission. Dependencies must also be available through that repository.

steps.note: The tested artifact coordinates are examples; specify your package. A separate consumer repository ensures the artifact is fetched over HTTP. Build/plugin dependencies may come from Maven Central unless mirrored by your policy.

limitations: Virtual deployment is deliberately omitted; deploy directly to the authorized local member.
Client checksums remain strict (-C). A dependency already in consumer-m2 is not evidence of remote retrieval.

contains: <maven> deploys a release and a snapshot twice
Scenario: Maven resolves release, parent, transitive and both snapshot forms cold and during an upstream outage
